To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have built an NLP system based on a linguistically motivated grammar, which is capable of analysing a billion-word corpus in less than 4 days, and that this system is robust enough to be useful for real-world applications.

(a) CCG is an appropriate formalism for the representation of syntactic and semantic information; (b) C&C is an efficient, robust, and linguistically motivated system for the analysis of large amounts of language; and (c) Boxer is a robust and linguistically motivated module for the production of interpretable semantic representations from CCG derivations.
we have built an NLP system that can process 1 billion words of text in 5 days on 18 processors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing efficient and accurate NLP tools for the large-scale statistical modelling of natural language.
building NLP systems that are robust, efficient, and linguistically accurate.
the development of a complete system for large-scale NLP, based on a linguistically motivated formalism, which can be used to process a wide range of tasks and domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C&C has the ability to produce high quality linguistic analysis of large corpora, at high speeds, using only a small amount of hardware.
C&C is a system that can analyse a billion words of text in a linguistically motivated and linguistically accurate manner in a matter of days on a modest number of processors.
C&C and Boxers are very good at what they do and are a good combination of tools for the job.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the only group that has been able to analyse a billion words with a linguistically motivated system, and that we have done so in a matter of days.

the C&C tools have been used for a wide variety of applications, ranging from the automatic analysis of the entire Gigawood corpus (1 billion tokens) (Clark et al., 2010; Clark and Curran, in press) to the analysis of large corpora of speech (Curran and O’Dwyer, 2010) and to the analysis of text from the Web and other sources (Clark and Curram, 2010).
we are able to analyse a large corpus with a linguistically motivated parser and produce interpretable semantic representations in a few days.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to develop a system which combines a high degree of linguistic coverage with high speed.
linguistically motivated large scale NLP is now possible.
it is possible to combine a highly expressive formalism with a highly engineered implementation to produce a system which is both linguistically accurate and highly scalable.
